summary: Teams participate in a virtual investment simulation, managing a $100,000 portfolio by investing in stocks, mutual funds, and bonds. The top teams create a multimedia presentation explaining their investment strategies, choices, and performance, and answer judges' questions in a videoconference. Teams must follow specific investment rules and submit their entry by the deadline to be eligible.
time_limits: Setup: no more than three (3) minutes
Presentation: no more than ten (10) minutes
Judges’ questions: no more than five (5) minutes
Presentation WILL BE STOPPED AT TEN (10) MINUTES
submission_requirements: Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Team ID cannot be accepted
The team is responsible for securing a BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including themselves, whose image or work is used in the project
The team is responsible for citing all sources, including themselves, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: Event registration deadline is no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
Teams must purchase at least $8,000-$10,000 of shares in at least 5 different stocks each in a different industry by 3:59 pm ET on Friday, December 19, 2026
Teams MUST purchase and hold $10,000 in mutual funds by 3:59 pm ET on Friday, December 19, 2026
Teams MUST make a minimum of six purchases by December 19th to be eligible for placement
competencies: Research and analyze various investment options, evaluating cash and asset allocation strategies to maximize return within given restrictions
Calculate investment amounts and return on investments, applying relevant formulas and financial concepts to assess performance and value
Manage an online investment fund, applying real-world decision-making to monitor and adjust holdings over time
Determine the timing of buying and selling investments by interpreting market trends, economic indicators, and relevant financial factors
Prepare investment reports using spreadsheet software to organize, calculate, and present financial data in a clear and professional format
Develop and deliver a presentation of investment strategies, communicating findings, rationale, and recommendations to a professional audience

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Introduction is engaging; summary clearly reinforces key insights.
Strategy is well-justified and shows strong grasp of investment principles and goals.
Technical terms are used precisely and effectively, with clear, insightful explanations that enhance understanding.
The strategy and research reflect strong financial expertise, with thorough, well-supported analysis and clear insight.
Visual elements are polished, well-balanced, and enhance the message with strong visual appeal and clarity.
Delivery is polished and engaging, with strong vocal presence, precise diction, and consistent, natural eye contact.
Responses are confident, detailed, and insightful.

judging_notes: Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary or postsecondary contestant may enter this event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state
Teams who do not submit an entry following the topic listed below or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified
Teams participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible
